This is close to a direct rediscovery of the well-documented earnings-management-around-equity-issuance result (Teoh-Welch-Wong, plus the Sloan accrual and Pontiff-Woodgate issuance anomalies), and mechanically the variable is exactly zero for the large majority of firms (non-issuers and non-gated firms), so decile sorts will be dominated by ties and the "long leg" carries no economic content.

Because net payout/assets is almost always far smaller than operating cash flow/assets, the MIN will equal the payout term for the overwhelming majority of firms, so the "complementarity" is mechanically inert and the signal collapses into the known net-payout-yield anomaly.

Persistence-weighted payout interacted with durable cash profitability is a defensible non-additive construct, but the 0-5 integer multiplier means cross-sectional variation is largely driven by cash-based operating profitability (a published anomaly), non-repurchasers pile up at exactly zero regardless of quality, and negative-OCF persistent repurchasers land in the extreme short leg by accident of sign rather than design.

Testing the second moment of financing flows is a legitimately new dimension and the sign logic is correct, but the doubly-ranked non-negative product saturates at zero for any firm with decent cash flow or stable financing, so the long leg will be a large tied mass and the spread will be driven almost entirely by the short leg — plus the five-year VOL window will bite into coverage.

This is the archive's leading kinked-financing signal with the sole change of a one-year-lagged asset deflator — a cosmetic measurement variant whose economic content is identical, and since both the financing flow and the quality leg are re-scaled by the same lagged base, the cross-sectional ranks will be near-collinear with the original, so the test has little power to teach anything new.

Adding financing-policy consistency to the credibility weight is an economically distinct and defensible upgrade to the leading kink structure rather than a rescaling, though the reviewer should note that five-year financing volatility is mechanically correlated with the magnitude of the current financing flow, so the weight will systematically shrink precisely the largest observations in both legs.

This is literally a sub-expression of the already-evaluated channel-specific kink (and a close relative of the gen-0 quality-gated net payout), so it is an ablation diagnostic rather than a new signal, and its result is largely predictable from the two existing tests that already bracket it.

This is the sign-flipped version of the gen-3 working-capital signal that failed at t=−2.64, re-rationalized after the fact, and the claim that the current-ratio change is "not mechanically linked to the financing inflow" is wrong — issuance proceeds land in current assets, so the signal largely reduces to going long the biggest raisers, contradicting the well-documented external-financing effect.

The stated logic contradicts the expression: RANK(NEG(sales growth)) is *largest* for shrinking firms, so capital-returning shrinking firms occupy the extreme long leg rather than being "scored near neutral," meaning the trade is driven by a different (and less defensible) economic claim than the hypothesis states, on top of being close to the known net-external-financing/asset-growth complex.

This is the gen-4 conjunctive kink with the leverage leg swapped for share-count growth, and the "independent verification" claim is weakened by the fact that csho growth is mechanically driven by the same sstk/prstkc flows already in the signal, so the MIN weight partly restates the conditioning variable rather than validating it.

Averaging oancf/at with its own first difference inside an already-tested kink is a cosmetic weight tweak, and the orthogonality claim is wrong — DELTA(oancf/at,1) contains the current level with a positive loading, so this is close to a rescaled version of the existing level-weighted kink.

Redefining the flow as pure net shareholder payout (a real scope change, not a weight swap, and close to but not identical with published net-payout-yield work since it is asset-scaled and quality-kinked), though the reviewer should note that adding always-nonnegative dvt shifts the zero threshold so the indicator will largely partition dividend payers from non-payers rather than capital returners from raisers.

The weight RANK(NEG((ib-oancf)/at)) is mechanically dominated by oancf and therefore is largely a re-parameterization of the already-tested cash-profitability weight in the identical kink structure, so it cannot deliver the claimed independence from the profitability channel.

Earnings volatility is a genuinely distinct (second-moment) conditioning dimension not yet used inside the kink, and the diagnosis of why the gen-0 weakest-link version failed is credible, though this remains the Nth weight substitution in a heavily mined structural family and coverage will suffer from the 5-year window.

Replacing oancf with MA(oancf,3) in an already-tested ratio is precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and it does not address the more likely cause of the alpha/FMB gap — the exploding, sign-unstable behavior of the ratio when the denominator floor binds.

The clean-surplus reconstruction (ΔCEQ − retained earnings + Δdebt) is essentially the published Richardson–Sloan net external financing measure, but here it is deployed as a deliberate measurement/coverage test that holds the interaction structure fixed, and with coverage stuck at 0.079 across the entire family this is the single most informative diagnostic on offer — the main risk is that ΔCEQ absorbs OCI and acquisition currency, blurring the kink point.

This is a mechanical SUMRANK ensemble of two signals already in the archive whose components are analytically nested (the "surprise" is the level minus its own moving average, so the two are strongly correlated by construction), adding no new economic content and amounting to the cosmetic combination the objective explicitly discourages.

Putting the bounded dependence ratio inside the asymmetric structure is a defensible scaling change with a real outlier-control argument, but oancf now appears in both the flow denominator and the quality weight, so the two legs double-count cash generation and any improvement will be hard to attribute; magnitude compression also risks killing the alpha that came from asset-scaled dollar size.

This is a pure lookback-horizon parameter sweep on the incumbent kink with no new economic mechanism; the 1-year-versus-5-year gap is informative to know, but interpolating one knob setting is low-value knob-turning rather than a substantively different improvement.

The expression correctly implements the stated hypothesis (the indicator fires exactly when oancf<0 and roughly doubles the short-leg weight there) and a discrete-state non-linearity in the weight is a genuine departure from the family's smooth ranks, though the incremental effect is likely small since negative-OCF firms already sit near the top of RANK(NEG(oancf/at)), and the isolated short leg risks simply reloading on the distress/profitability tail that RMW already spans.

The diagnosis is sharp and correct — industry-demeaning the flow shifts the zero threshold that defines the kink, contaminating the gen-3 result — so isolating the peer adjustment to the credibility weight alone is a well-identified decomposition with a sound economic rationale rather than a cosmetic re-specification.

This is a mechanical stacking of three already-tested refinements (capacity normalization, IND_RANK quality, burn indicator) that individually produced near-identical statistics (alpha ~3.1–3.3%, t ~2.6–2.8) and are almost certainly highly collinear, so it offers no new economic mechanism and its outcome will be uninterpretable as to which element matters.

The stated motivation collapses under its own numbers — the two measurement routes already cover 0.079 and 0.084 and both legs still require oancf for the quality weight, so the union can add at most a percent or two of sample, making this a data-plumbing patch rather than an economically motivated signal.

This is the archive's "Cash-burn amplified stress kink" with RANK swapped for IND_RANK (or equivalently the "Peer-relative quality" kink plus the burn dummy), a two-knob recombination of components already tested at t≈2.6–2.84, and its value as an ablation of Proposal 1 does not make it a substantively different hypothesis.

Substituting MA(3) for the one-year oancf weight inside an otherwise unchanged incumbent kink is a single smoothing-parameter tweak, not a new interaction, and the archive already shows that smoothing the quality weight (and the flow) in this family degrades rather than improves alpha.

Assigning different measurement horizons to the payout and issuance legs is a genuinely structural asymmetry with a defensible rationale (programme-like buybacks vs. event-like raises), but the construction is flawed in that the two indicators no longer partition the sample — a firm with MA<0 and current-year raise loads on both legs while the reverse case loads on neither — so results will be partly driven by that overlap rather than by horizon per se.

Weighting the payout leg by funding capacity (costly-signalling) and the issuance leg by earnings opacity (adverse selection) is an economically coherent, leg-specific pairing that is distinct from both the symmetric earnings-stability kink and the symmetric uncertainty amplifier in the archive, and it offers a testable diagnosis of why the latter had a strong FMB slope but negligible alpha.

This is a mechanical bolt-together of two already-tested archive components (the gen-7 maintenance-adjusted flow and the gen-6 negative-oancf discontinuity) with no new economic content, and since both were evaluated on the same 0.078-coverage sample with near-identical alphas, the combination is far more likely to reshuffle the same firms than to reveal an independent effect.

A straight swap of one archived credibility weight (act/lct, gen 7) onto another archived flow definition (dp-adjusted, gen 7) is a cosmetic recombination, and the stated coverage rationale is wrong — the flow still requires sstk/prstkc/dltis/dltr, so the sample will remain bound near 0.078 rather than inheriting the liquidity variant's 0.103.

Replacing oancf/at with (oancf−dp)/at inside the credibility rank is a near-collinear reparameterization of the gen-1 baseline kink — dp/at is a slow-moving industry characteristic, so the cross-sectional rank will shift only modestly — making this too trivial a perturbation to justify a test slot.

This is a plumbing patch rather than an economic hypothesis, and it is internally compromised: dp already enters the flow term, so the ib+dp fallback weight shares a component with the signal it is meant to condition, inducing mechanical correlation in exactly the firm-years the fallback is supposed to add.

The within-firm normalization is the most genuinely novel idea in this batch and the RMW/CMA-spanning diagnosis is sound, but the expression is internally inconsistent — the short leg uses NEG(TS_RANK(·)), which is negative-valued, so after the outer SUB capital raisers receive a *positive* score that increases with their own-history cash flow, exactly reversing the stated hypothesis (the archive's working form uses a rank of the negated quality, not the negation of the rank).

This is a legitimate specification correction rather than a cosmetic variant — basing both indicators on the current-year flow restores a clean, exhaustive partition so the horizon asymmetry is actually identified — though novelty is modest and the reviewer should note that firms currently returning capital with a positive three-year average flow will contribute negatively to the long leg, so the leg is not monotone in payout.

This is a pure denominator tweak on the archive's leading consumption-scaled kink (dp → dp+dvt), with no new economic mechanism and a change that bites only for dividend payers, so it is a cosmetic parameter variant rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

The negative-oancf discontinuity was already tested on the asset-scaled kink and produced ls_talpha 2.838 versus 2.820 baseline — a difference indistinguishable from noise that the reasoning nonetheless cites as evidence — so grafting it onto the new denominator is recombination of two known elements with no credible incremental prior.

Internally inconsistent: the hypothesis argues that scaling the *flow* by depreciation induces a capital-intensity/sector tilt, but the expression industry-adjusts only the quality *weight* (a change already tested and slightly inferior in gen 6) and leaves the allegedly tilted flow entirely market-wide, so the stated problem is not addressed by the stated fix.

Both ingredients are already in the archive and the conjunctive weight previously delivered lower alpha and t-alpha than the simple oancf weight (0.031/2.66 vs 0.033/2.82), so the only motivation is a marginally higher Sharpe, which makes this a plausible but noise-driven crossing rather than a new mechanism.

The credibility weight is genuinely new — a post-distribution internal-equity flow (ΔRE ≈ ib − dvt) rather than another cash or balance-sheet level — and it tests a distinct "was the payout actually funded" mechanism, though its likely high correlation with profitability/oancf weights means the incremental evidence should be judged against the existing leader rather than in isolation.

The proposal correctly diagnoses why the gen-5 total-distribution kink failed and re-tests the broader distribution scope with an economically motivated non-zero threshold, but it should be flagged in interpretation that shifting the threshold by dp assigns most zero-financing firms to the "stress" leg with magnitude dp/at, which risks mislabeling ordinary capital-intensive firms as funding-stressed.
